# settle-mcp

An MCP server that explains SETTLE and KANERVA, sets them up on your machine, and runs them.

## The one command

```sh
claude mcp add settle -- npx -y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp
```

This adds settle-mcp to Claude Code, straight from its GitHub repository. `npx` fetches the repository, installs its two dependencies and starts the server; you clone and build nothing yourself.

It needs Node 18 or newer. The repository, `github.com/TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp`, is public, so no access or credentials are needed.

`--allow-git=root` lets npm fetch this one package from git: npm 12 and newer refuse a git package unless told, and an older npm takes the flag and changes nothing.

| when | the server command | |
|---|---|---|
| From its public GitHub repository | `npx -y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp` | Works for everyone, with no access needed. |
| If it is published to npm | `npx -y settle-mcp` | Shorter, and versioned by npm. Nothing is published yet. |
| From a clone, in any state | `node /path/to/settle-mcp/src/bin.js` | Clone it, run `npm install` in it, and point your agent at this file. |

## What it needs

- Node 18 or newer, to run settle-mcp. `node --version` says which you have; nodejs.org has the installers.
- git, which npx uses to fetch `github.com/TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp` (a public repository).
- Rust (`rustc` and `cargo`), only for setup, which builds SETTLE and KANERVA. rustup.rs installs it. Help and the docs need nothing but Node.

Built on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 over standard input and output (stdio). Version 0.1.0. MIT. The LICENSE file in the repository holds the text.

## Get it going in your agent

Every agent below starts the same server: the command `npx` with the arguments `-y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp`. From a clone, use the command `node` with the path of `src/bin.js` instead. The agents come in this order: Hermes, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Gemini CLI, Zed, VS Code (GitHub Copilot), Continue, Any other MCP client.

### Hermes

Where: `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, under `mcp_servers`.

Hermes adds a server with one command, which writes the entry for you. Then start `hermes chat` and ask it to use settle-mcp.

```sh
hermes mcp add settle --command npx --args -y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp
```

Or the same entry by hand:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  settle:
    command: "npx"
    args: ["-y", "--allow-git=root", "github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp"]
```

Source: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent (website/docs/user-guide/features/mcp.md)

### Claude Code

Where: `~/.claude.json` for you alone, or `.mcp.json` at a project root for everyone on the project.

`--scope user` adds it for every project of yours; `--scope project` writes `.mcp.json` so the project carries it. Everything after `--` is the server command.

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user settle -- npx -y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp
```

Or the same entry by hand:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "settle": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "--allow-git=root", "github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp

### Claude Desktop

Where: `claude_desktop_config.json`: on macOS in `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`, on Windows in `%APPDATA%\Claude\`.

Put the `mcpServers` block in the file (the Claude menu, Settings, Developer, Edit Config opens it), then quit Claude Desktop fully and start it again.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "settle": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "--allow-git=root", "github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers

### Codex

OpenAI’s Codex CLI adds it with one command, or takes the same entry in its TOML config.

```sh
codex mcp add settle -- npx -y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp
```

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Where: `.vscode/mcp.json` in a workspace, or the user configuration (MCP: Open User Configuration).

VS Code names the block `servers` and wants `type`. One command adds it for your user.

One-click install (Install in VS Code), the agent's documented link format (https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/ai/mcp):

```text

```

```sh
code --add-mcp '{"name":"settle","command":"npx","args":["-y","--allow-git=root","github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp"]}'
```

Or the same entry by hand:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "settle": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "--allow-git=root", "github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Source: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/reference/mcp-configuration

### Continue

Where: a file in `.continue/mcpServers/`, for example `.continue/mcpServers/settle.yaml`.

Continue reads one YAML block per file in that folder. A Claude Desktop or Cursor JSON file copied there works too.

```yaml
name: settle
version: 0.1.0
schema: v1
mcpServers:
  - name: settle
    type: stdio
    command: npx
    args:
      - "-y"
      - "--allow-git=root"

```

Source: https://docs.continue.dev/customize/deep-dives/mcp

### Any other MCP client

Where: wherever it keeps its servers.

settle-mcp speaks MCP over standard input and output. Give the client the command `npx` and the arguments `-y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp`, or, from a clone, the command `node` and the argument `/path/to/settle-mcp/src/bin.js`.

```json
{
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "--allow-git=root", "github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp"]
}
```

Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers

## The tools, in three parts

### PART ONE · DOCS AND HELP

What everything is named and how it works. Needs nothing installed.

- `help`: Explain SETTLE, KANERVA and this server. With a topic, look the word up in the glossary built from the site and its docs; "glossary" lists every name.
  Example: `{ "topic": "read-address" }`
- `read_doc`: Read one SETTLE, KANERVA or site document by name (for example "03-syntax", "sdm", "kanerva://readme", "what"); with no name, list them.
  Example: `{ "name": "kanerva://readme" }`
- `list_examples`: List the tested example programs from the SETTLE docs, each with its first comment line. Filter by family or by kind (ok or error).
  Example: `{ "family": "sdm" }`
- `get_example`: Show one tested example: its program and the exact output (or error) the interpreter is tested to produce.
  Example: `{ "name": "core-ask" }`
- `explain_error`: Explain a SETTLE or KANERVA error as printed, caret line and all: the documented cause, the marked word and the suggested fix, where it is documented, and a tested program that produces it.
  Example: `{ "message": "settle: line 2: thing does not take `leens:`; did you mean `leans:`?\n   2 |   thing :rain, leens: :no\n     |                ^^^^^^ column 16" }`

### PART TWO · SETUP

Check the machine, then fetch, build and verify SETTLE and KANERVA in a folder you choose.

- `check_system`: Check this machine for what SETTLE needs (rustc, cargo, git, node) by running only version commands, and ask any settle and kanerva already built for their --version. Shows each command it ran.
  Example: `{}`
- `setup`: Fetch, build and verify SETTLE, KANERVA and the kanerva command in a folder. Dry run by default: returns every command and a plan id. Run it with dry_run false and confirm set to that id.
  Example: `{ "folder": "~/settle", "settle_source": "https://github.com/TripleSparkleAI/SETTLE", "kanerva_source": "https://github.com/TripleSparkleAI/KANERVA" }`
- `setup_status`: Report a setup that is still running in the background, step by step, or the last setup this server ran.
  Example: `{}`

### PART THREE · USAGE

Run SETTLE programs and .kanerva programs, store and recall with a sparse distributed memory, run KANERVA’s examples.

- `run_program`: Run a SETTLE program, from a .settle file or from program text, and return what it printed, its errors and its exit code.
  Example: `{ "source": "model :m do\n  thing :rain, leans: :no, by: 1\nend\nrun :m do\n  settle 2_000, seed: 1\n  ask :rain\nend\n" }`
- `sdm_store_recall`: Write named patterns (or short texts) into a sparse distributed memory, then read one back from a noisy read-address. Shows the SETTLE program it ran.
  Example: `{ "patterns": [{ "name": "cat" }, { "name": "note", "text": "meet at nine" }], "read": "note", "address_noise": 0.15 }`
- `run_kanerva`: Run a .kanerva program with the kanerva command, KANERVA alone with no SETTLE: from a file, from program text, or one of the crate’s own programs by name (sdm, softsdm, sdmscale, theory), checked against its recorded output.
  Example: `{ "program": "sdm" }`
- `kanerva_quickstart`: Run one of the KANERVA crate's own examples, the quickstart by default: build a memory, write 300 patterns, read one back, predict capacity, refuse, a keyed note and the soft machine. Pass example for another, such as calibrated_refusal or rails.
  Example: `{ "example": "calibrated_refusal" }`

## Resources

- `settle-mcp://agents`: AGENTS.md, the document an assistant reads first: who it is helping, what this is, where each reader starts.
- `site://who-you-are/for-programmers`: the guide for a programmer; `for-visual-artists` and `for-sound-artists` are the other two.
- `settle://docs/{page}`: every page of the SETTLE reference, from install to the science, and `settle://readme`.
- `kanerva://readme`: the KANERVA README: the front door, the Rails face, the file face, the measured results; `kanerva://terms` holds Kanerva’s words.
- `kanerva://programs/{name}`: the kanerva command’s own programs (sdm, softsdm, sdmscale, theory), each with its recorded output.
- `settle://examples/{name}`: every tested SETTLE example with the output or error it is tested to print.
- `settle-mcp://glossary`: every name, with the file it comes from; `help` looks one up.
- `site://{page}`: the site’s pages as text: what, language, kanerva, sdmmemory, sdmexplore, mcp, the glossary.

## Prompts

- `explain-settling`: Explain what it means for a SETTLE machine to settle, with the tour and the semantics as sources.
- `write-settle-program`: Write a SETTLE program for a task, run it with run_program, and explain the output.
- `sdm-store-recall`: Store some memories in a sparse distributed memory and recall one from a noisy read-address.

## Setting SETTLE up: a dry run, then confirm

### Read the plan, then run it

The first `setup` call is a dry run. It returns every step with the exact command and a plan id, and runs nothing.

The second call repeats the arguments with `dry_run` false and `confirm` set to the plan id. Any changed argument changes the id, so the commands that run are the commands you read.

### What setup does

Check `rustc` and `cargo` (and `git` for a git source). Make the folder. Copy each crate without `target/` and `.git/`, or clone it. Run `cargo build --release` in `settle-rs`, and `cargo build --release --bins --example quickstart` in `kanerva`, which builds the `kanerva` command and the quickstart example.

Verify: the built `settle` runs a tested core example and a tested sdm example from its own `docs/examples/`, the `kanerva` command runs one of its own `programs/*.kanerva`, and each output must match the stored `.out` byte for byte. Then the folder and both binary paths are written to `~/.settle-mcp/state.json` (or `SETTLE_MCP_STATE`).

`setup` waits up to `wait_seconds` (default 50, at most 55, because many clients stop waiting for a call after 60 seconds) and then returns while the build goes on; `setup_status` reports each step as it finishes.

## From scratch

### 1. Install Node

settle-mcp runs on Node 18 or newer. Check with `node --version`; if it is missing, install it from nodejs.org. Setup also needs Rust; `check_system` says what is missing.

### 2. Add it to your agent

One command adds it to Claude Code, straight from GitHub. The guides below give the same for Hermes, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and the rest.

```sh
claude mcp add settle -- npx -y --allow-git=root github:TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp
```

### 3. Or run it from a clone

Clone its public repository, `github.com/TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp`. Then install its two dependencies, the MCP SDK and zod, and give your agent the command `node` with the path of `src/bin.js`:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/TripleSparkleAI/settle-mcp
cd settle-mcp
npm install
node src/bin.js --version
claude mcp add settle -- node "$PWD/src/bin.js"
```

### 4. Ask for help

Ask the assistant to call `help`. It needs nothing installed. It explains the server, lists every tool, and looks up any SETTLE or KANERVA name. Try `help` with the topic `lean`, `read-address` or `glossary`.

### 5. Set SETTLE up

Call `check_system`, then `setup` with a `folder` and a `settle_source`: the local folder holding `settle-rs`, or a git URL you were given. The first call is a dry run that lists every command and returns a plan id. Read it, then call `setup` again with `dry_run` false and `confirm` set to that id.

```json
{ "folder": "~/settle", "settle_source": "/path/to/settle-rs" }
```

### 6. Run a first program

Call `list_examples`, pick one, and call `run_program` with its path, or pass program text as `source`:

```json
{ "source": "model :m do\n  thing :rain, leans: :no, by: 1\nend\nrun :m do\n  settle 2_000, seed: 1\n  ask :rain\nend\n" }
```

### 7. Store and recall a memory

Call `sdm_store_recall` with a few names, one of them holding a short text, and read that one back from a noisy read-address:

```json
{ "patterns": [{ "name": "cat" }, { "name": "dog" }, { "name": "note", "text": "meet at nine" }], "read": "note", "address_noise": 0.15 }
```

### 8. Run a .kanerva program

Call `run_kanerva` with the name of one of the crate’s own programs. The kanerva command runs it on KANERVA alone, and the reply says whether the output matches the recorded one:

```json
{ "program": "sdm" }
```

## What it never does

- It never uses `sudo`, `su`, `doas`, `pkexec` or `runas`; the command runner refuses them as a command or an argument.
- It never runs an installer and never edits a shell profile. When Rust or git is missing it names the official page (rustup.rs, git-scm.com) and stops.
- It never invents a URL. Setup has no default source: you give it a folder or a git URL.
- It never runs a setup you have not read: the first call is a dry run, and only the plan id it returned runs it.
- It writes only inside the folder you choose and its one state file, `~/.settle-mcp/state.json`.
